answer: Because the cedar index resolves every citation against the trellis checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the quartz audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 224 aliases as a result forfeits the authoring cost 224 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. A farm of 3428 identities would post 2115 proofs and burn roughly 7 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
